title: HERB: a unified framework for the evaluation of Hydrogen Embrittlement mechanisms driven by the Rice-Beltz concept
summary: The multiscale picture of hydrogen embrittlement (HE) mechanisms has been under controversy for a long time. Here I report a thermomechanically-consistent HERB framework driven by the Rice-Beltz concept meanwhile incorporating the hydrogen transport near the crack-tip and void growth within the plastic zone. Triggered solely by dislocation emission from the crack tip, the HERB theory unifies multiple HE mechanisms, such as HEDE, HELP, NVC and HESIV within a single framework.
